2026-04-12 21:54 UTC: No credible NSA mind control program exists; the only "news" is a satirical article presenting fictional claims.[2]

The search results contain one source—a Lawfare article—describing an alleged NSA program called "MINDPRISM" that supposedly extracts thoughts via dental implants and satellites.[2] However, this article is presented as satire, evidenced by absurdist details: it references "buxom Ukrainian nurses Qadhafi was thinking about" and claims "Kim Jong Un really is obsessed with basketball" as intelligence findings.[2] The article explicitly states it was published "at the request of the NSA" with technical details withheld, a hallmark of parody rather than genuine reporting.[2]

**Actual recent NSA news** focuses on legitimate security matters: warnings about Russian GRU router exploits (April 7, 2026), Zero Trust Implementation Guidelines (January 30, 2026), and alerts about pro-Russia hacktivist groups targeting critical infrastructure (December 9, 2025).[4]

The only substantive mind control history involves the **CIA**, not the NSA. A December 23, 2024, scholarly collection documents the CIA's historical MKULTRA, BLUEBIRD, and ARTICHOKE programs, which conducted experiments using drugs, hypnosis, isolation, and sensory deprivation on human subjects.[1] This represents declassified past conduct, not new NSA developments.[1]

Declassified reports do show the NSA violated surveillance rules and conducted mass surveillance under Section 702, but these involve communications interception, not mind control.[5][6]
